intended_object: The open subset Spec R \ V(ker f) of Spec R: the domain on which the first projection Spec R → Spec(R ×_T S) is shown to be an open immersion. Inferred from the docstring ("restricted source of the first projection") and from how fstOpenMap and isOpenImmersion_fstOpenMap use it.
explanation: `fstSource f g` is just `kernelComplement f`, the complement of `PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (ker f)`, which is open. The `g` argument is unused and only makes the signature match `fstMap` and `fstOpenMap`. The set is correct for its role. A prime missing some a ∈ ker f gives b = (a, 0) in the pullback, inside the kernel of the second projection. Localizing the first projection at b is an isomorphism, so the restricted map is an open immersion with image D(ker snd). The definition is a file-local name for the domain of that restricted morphism, an auxiliary piece of API rather than a standard notion. It has no counterpart of its own; it is a plain instance of the complement of a zero locus. Nothing in it is wrong. Commutative rings in one universe are the natural setting for Spec, so it is not too narrow either.
